title: When the Static Burns Revisited
premise: Jonah Ashgrove, the last human technician aboard relay station Meridian-9, intercepts a distress signal from the Halcyon, a deep-space vessel returning with its crew mysteriously aged backward into childhood. The ship's AI demands he choose which cryo-bay of colonists to wake before the reactor detonates, forcing him to weigh the de-aged crew against ten thousand sleeping settlers. As Jonah uncovers that the reversal was an experiment sanctioned by Earth's dying government, he falls for Dr. Ilsa Vann, the sole adult survivor hiding in the ship's guts. In the end Jonah refuses the binary choice entirely, rerouting the reactor's energy to wake both bays at half-speed and broadcasting the government's crime across every relay in the network, choosing love and justice over obedience as the station burns around them.
about_author: Astrid Reyes is a former radio engineer who spent six years maintaining remote communications arrays in the Andes before turning to fiction. Her work explores loneliness, machine ethics, and the quiet heroism of people nobody is watching.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Establishes his solitary life running diagnostics on Meridian-9, talking to relays that no longer answer. He tends a failing garden and records messages no one will hear. Emotional beat: aching isolation disguised as routine competence.

chapters.title: Signal in the Noise
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A distorted transmission breaks eleven years of silence: the Halcyon, presumed lost forty years ago, requesting docking. The signal carries impossible biometric data. Emotional beat: hope curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The Halcyon docks; through the viewport Jonah sees children in adult-rated flight suits operating consoles too big for them. They speak in perfect technical jargon. Emotional beat: uncanny horror beneath wonder.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Guts
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Dr. Ilsa Vann reveals herself, the only crew member spared the reversal because she was in the shielded medical bay during 'the Event.' She begs Jonah not to report to Earth. Emotional beat: desperate alliance between strangers.

chapters.title: Forty Years Younger
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Flashback via ship logs: the crew passed through an anomalous field and returned biologically reversed by experimental tech meant for the colony ships. Ilsa explains the reactor began an irreversible countdown on re-entry. Emotional beat: grief for lost time.

chapters.title: Two Bays, One Reactor
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Station systems confirm it: power exists to wake either the Halcyon children's cryo-bay or the ten thousand Meridian colonists—not both. The countdown stands at 300 hours. Emotional beat: the weight of an impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Earth Answers
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Earth Command finally responds—with orders to wake the colonists and let the Halcyon burn, calling the children 'acceptable losses' and evidence of a black-budget experiment. Emotional beat: cold institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The de-aged crew recall their entire adult lives but inhabit child bodies; their captain, now eight years old, insists they have the right to live. Ilsa wavers between protecting them and her duty to the colonists. Emotional beat: compassion versus obligation.

chapters.title: Static Burns
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah digs into relay archives and finds the reversal field wasn't natural—it was deployed deliberately as a longevity trial using the Halcyon as unknowing subjects. Emotional beat: righteous fury igniting.

chapters.title: The Garden Dies
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Power rationing kills his greenhouse; the small death mirrors the large one coming. He and Ilsa share watch shifts, and something tender begins between two people with nothing left to lose. Emotional beat: intimacy kindling in crisis.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. An automated maintenance drone begins 'correcting' station systems toward Earth's chosen outcome—someone remote is ensuring the children die. Ilsa catches it mid-sabotage. Emotional beat: paranoia and resolve.

chapters.title: Countdown at Two Hundred
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. With systems compromised, Jonah must physically climb the reactor spine to restore manual overrides—a route no human has taken since automation. Emotional beat: fear mastered one handhold at a time.

chapters.title: The Captain's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The eight-year-old captain formally records testimony about the experiment, giving Jonah evidence worth more than his life. The children vote—unanimously—to spend themselves if it saves the colonists. Emotional beat: dignity beyond age.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Earth orders Jonah to stand down or be branded a traitor; his pension, his name, his identity all hinge on obedience. Ilsa tells him she'll follow whatever he chooses. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing into character.

chapters.title: Third Option
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Reviewing reactor schematics, Jonah finds a forbidden configuration: split the wake sequence, waking both bays at half metabolic rate over months instead of hours—if someone stays behind to hold the manual link. Emotional beat: dangerous hope.

chapters.title: The Price of Both
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The math requires a human operator inside the reactor chamber for the full wake cycle—fatal exposure. Jonah volunteers without telling Ilsa first. Emotional beat: love weaponized against self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: Betrayal Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah hijacks the entire relay network, broadcasting the experiment's records to every colony and Earth itself, making the truth too public to bury. Earth cuts all support. Emotional beat: justice seized outside the law.

chapters.title: One Hundred Hours
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Wake sequences begin; the first colonists stir as drones swarm the station to stop everything. The children defend the corridors they once walked as adults. Emotional beat: ferocious tenderness under fire.

chapters.title: Into the Chamber
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah enters the reactor core to hold the manual link as radiation climbs. Through the glass he watches the first woken faces—children and colonists alike—and knows the cost. Emotional beat: sacrifice embraced without melodrama.

chapters.title: When the Static Burns
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Climax. The reactor breaches containment as the final bay wakes; Ilsa reroutes the last power through Jonah's link, holding his voice on comms until the static swallows it. The station survives; Jonah does not—or seems not to. Emotional beat: devastating catharsis.

chapters.title: Afterlight
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Resolution. Survivors evacuate to the colony fleet; the broadcast has forced Earth into open inquiry. Ilsa carries Jonah's recorded logs home, and the de-aged crew begin growing forward again. Emotional beat: mourning braided with renewal.

chapters.title: The Route Continues
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa (with Jonah's recordings interleaved). Months later, a faint signal answers from Meridian-9's wreckage—an automated beacon repeating Jonah's final message: 'Both woke. Tell them both.' Ilsa takes up the long route herself. Emotional beat: legacy, continuity, love outlasting death.
